items.stem: A Pod must run a short setup task that copies files into a shared volume before the main application container starts. Which construct runs that task to completion first?

options.rationale: Correct: init containers run to completion in order before app containers start, making them ideal for setup tasks.
A sidecar runs alongside the main container for its whole life, not to completion beforehand.
A liveness probe checks health of a running container; it does not run setup work.
A CronJob schedules whole Pods on a timetable; it is not an in-Pod setup step.

items.explanation: Correct: init containers run to completion in order before app containers start, making them ideal for setup tasks.

items.stem: A container takes 40 seconds to warm up. Kubernetes keeps killing it during startup. Which probe should be added or tuned to stop the premature restarts?

options.rationale: Correct: a startup probe holds off the liveness probe until the app has finished its slow start.
A readiness probe removes the Pod from Service endpoints but does not stop liveness restarts.
Resource limits do not change probe timing or restart behaviour.
NetworkPolicies govern traffic, not container restart behaviour.

items.explanation: Correct: a startup probe holds off the liveness probe until the app has finished its slow start.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Kubernetes Secrets are correct by default? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Secret values are base64-encoded, not encrypted, unless encryption at rest is configured
options.rationale: Correct: by default Secrets are only base64-encoded in etcd.

options.text: A Secret can be mounted as a volume or exposed as environment variables
options.rationale: Correct: both consumption methods are supported.

options.text: Secrets are encrypted at rest automatically on every cluster
options.rationale: Encryption at rest must be explicitly configured; it is not automatic.

options.text: Secrets cannot be referenced by Pods in the same namespace
options.rationale: Pods reference Secrets in their own namespace routinely.

options.text: Secrets are stored only in the kubelet, never in etcd
options.rationale: Secrets are persisted in etcd via the API server.

items.explanation: Correct: by default Secrets are only base64-encoded in etcd.
